rules.replace: transforms from a car into a tall humanoid robot built from its own parts

The car starts to transform: its body panels split along their seams and slide apart, the wheels fold up and move to the shoulders, two legs unfold from underneath and push the body upright, the doors swing out to become the arms, the bonnet becomes the chest, and a robot head with two glowing white eyes rises between the shoulders. The robot stands up to its full height in the middle of the garage, facing the camera, and holds still at the end.
Mechanical clicks, whirring servos and heavy metal clanks as the parts move and lock into place, echoing in the concrete garage, then a low electric hum. No speech, no voice.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame and composition anchor for [Shot 1], defining the complete visible image exactly as supplied, including the framing, camera viewpoint, subject placement, subject scale, crop, foreground-to-background relationship, whatever forms the area behind and around the subject, lighting, shadows, colors, gradients, depth cues, and overall scene composition. Its rendering style, whether photographic, illustrated, stylised, or three-dimensional, is part of what is preserved.
<Subject 1> is [SUBJECT] defined by <Picture 1>. During the shot it [CHANGE], as shown at the end of the clip.
<Subject 2> is the complete visible area behind, beneath, beside, and around <Subject 1> as defined by <Picture 1>, preserving its exact colors, surfaces, objects if any are present, spatial layout, lighting, shadows, gradients, and depth. Whatever that area looks like in <Picture 1> is exactly what it looks like in the target video, including its overall tone and brightness, and it is never exchanged for a different kind of surrounding.

summary:
[keyframe completion] The target video begins from <Picture 1> and ends on the last frame: <Subject 1> [CHANGE] in one continuous fixed-camera shot, while the complete visible area represented by <Subject 2> stays the same.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the supplied image is the starting frame, retaining its viewpoint, framing, surroundings, lighting, and rendering style.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): transformed - it changes into what the last frame shows.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the referenced surroundings remain visually identical, with nothing substituted, added, or removed.

detailed_description:
The target video develops directly from the complete supplied image in <Picture 1>, preserving its rendering style, color treatment, lighting, composition, and full visible scene. <Picture 1> is the actual starting frame.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. The camera stays still at the same height for the whole clip, with no zoom and no pan. [ACTION] <Subject 2> remains stable throughout, with no transformation, replacement, recoloring, or change of location.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Makes a video that starts exactly on your first picture and ends exactly on your last one. H3 makes everything in between: here a car that turns into a robot.

 Steps

  1. 1. Pick how many seconds.
  2. 2. Load your first picture.
  3. 3. Load your last picture.
  4. 4. Leave the size at 1088 x 1920 (Full HD), or pick 704 x 1280 for a smaller card.
  5. 5. In Find and Replace, fill the four boxes (see below).
  6. 6. Seed: F (fixed) or R (random).
  7. Press Run.

 The two pictures

  • Use the same place and the same camera in both pictures, and change only the thing that should change. The easy way: make the first picture, then the last one as an edit of it (Flux Klein from workflow 01, or another edit model).
  • The demo pictures were made with Nano Banana Pro in Google Flow: the car first, then the robot as an edit of the car picture.
  • Both pictures need the same shape as the video (9:16 for Portrait): they are cropped from the centre to the video size.

 The four boxes

  • [SUBJECT]: what is in the first picture: the glossy cherry-red concept car.
  • [CHANGE]: what it becomes, in a few words: transforms from a car into a tall humanoid robot built from its own parts.
  • [ACTION]: HOW it changes, step by step, in order. The more concrete, the better the middle of the video.
  • [SOUND]: what you hear while it changes. End with No speech, no voice when nobody should talk.

 Good to know

  • In the tests (4 seeds) the car turned into the robot every time and the video ended on the robot picture.
  • Why not the 2K pass of workflow 25 here? In the tests it redrew the two pictures, so the video no longer started and ended exactly on them. This workflow keeps them exact.
  • Another seed gives another way of changing between the same two pictures.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your first picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns your two pictures into the model's own format, and the finished render into video frames.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA: 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Duration Pixaroma (1. how many seconds) - How many seconds the video lasts, from the first picture to the last one, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (2. the first frame) - Your first picture: the video starts exactly on it.
  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (3. the last frame) - Your last picture: the video ends exactly on it. Best: the same place and camera as the first picture, with only the thing that changes.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (4. video size) - The size of the video: 1088 x 1920 (Full HD, the default) or 704 x 1280 (faster, for smaller cards). Both pictures are cropped to it, so use pictures of the same shape. Portrait for Shorts, Landscape for YouTube.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (5. what it is, how it changes, the sound) - Four short boxes that fill the [SUBJECT], [CHANGE], [ACTION] and [SOUND] places of the prompt below. [ACTION] tells H3 HOW it changes, step by step.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the prompt, leave it) - The prompt in MiniMax's own layout: your first picture is the first frame, the last picture the end, and your boxes go into its places. Leave it as it is.
  • Seed Pixaroma (6. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Upscale Image (the first picture to the video size) - Brings the first picture to the exact video size (cropped from the centre, nothing stretched).
  • Upscale Image (the last picture to the video size) - Brings the last picture to the exact video size, so it can be the last frame.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your first picture) - Builds the empty video at your size and length and reads the prompt together with your first picture (<Picture 1>).
  • MiniMaxH3AddGuide (your last picture, last frame) - Puts your last picture at the LAST frame (frame_idx -1), so the video ends exactly on it.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.
  • VAE Decode Audio (the sound) - Turns the sound H3 made into audio for the saved video.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the video) - Saves the video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/First Last Frame with the sound H3 made, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Video size5 seconds
1088 x 1920 (Full HD), the defaultabout 2:30 (145 to 155 s)
704 x 1280about 1 min (55 s)

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
